solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Excitement of a geek about some cocaine

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the word for a geek is read backwards

parts.note: a geek is a nerd
a line is a measured dose of cocaine, so some of it is a line

explanation.surface: A nerd gets a thrill from a snort of cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns NERD into DREN; 'some cocaine' is A LINE, as in a line of the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: The hormone released in moments of thrill stands for the thrill itself, as in an adrenaline rush.

clue.text: Spot Mrs Fawlty in audition being versatile

indicators.note: in audition means as heard spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a spot is a fleck, and Mrs Fawlty is Sybil, Basil's wife in the BBC sitcom Fawlty Towers

explanation.surface: Someone spots Sybil Fawlty at an audition and finds her adaptable.
explanation.walkthrough: Fawlty Towers is a classic 1970s British TV comedy set in a hotel; Sybil is the hotelier's wife. FLECK SYBIL said quickly sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone versatile adapts easily, which is to be bendable or adaptable.

clue.text: New wounds caused bleeding hearts

indicators.note: the hearts of words are their central letters, taken from each of the three words before it

explanation.surface: Fresh injuries have left a sentimental soul's heart bleeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bleeding hearts' looks like a phrase, but 'bleeding' is the third word whose middle is taken: UN, US and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unused has never been employed, so it is still fresh or new.

clue.text: Ninety-nine received and understood

indicators.note: received means heard, so the Roman numeral is taken by its sound

parts.note: IC is a loose Roman numeral for ninety-nine, one before a hundred

explanation.surface: A radio operator acknowledges message ninety-nine: received and understood.
explanation.walkthrough: IC, spoken letter by letter, sounds like the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying I see is a spoken way of indicating that you have grasped something.

clue.text: TV producer calling one character at a time

definitions.meaning: Aaron ... was the American producer behind Dynasty and Charlie's Angels

definitions.text: calling one character at a time
definitions.meaning: naming the letters of a word one by one in order

explanation.surface: A television producer phones the cast members one at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: The producer's surname, and the act of saying a word's letters in order.

clue.text: Works in arid condition

indicators.note: in places the works inside the word for arid

parts.note: arid means dry
OPS is short for opuses, musical works

explanation.surface: A building site operating in a parched state.
explanation.definitionFit: An old medical name for swelling from fluid build-up, a bodily condition now called oedema.

clue.text: Find cheese, basil, salami at the back of the shop

indicators.note: at the back means the final letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Cheese, basil and salami can be found at the rear of the store.
explanation.definitionFit: A delicatessen is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: Vows left to false god

parts.note: I do is the vow made at a wedding

explanation.surface: Marriage promises abandoned for a false deity.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is an image worshipped as a deity, a false god in biblical terms.

clue.text: It's standard in Orkneys, perhaps, to be a curtain twitcher

indicators.note: in places standard inside the rearranged islands' name
perhaps says the letters of Orkneys are only one possible arrangement

parts.note: par is a standard or norm

explanation.surface: In the Orkney islands it is normal to be a nosy neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: A curtain twitcher is British slang for someone who peeps out at the neighbours from behind the curtains.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are idioms for a busybody who pries into other people's affairs.

clue.text: King rejecting the other king

indicators.note: rejecting means turning back, so the two words are read from end to start

parts.note: 'the other' is a coy British euphemism for sex
Rex is Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch turning down another monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' turns SEXREX round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerxes was a Persian king of the fifth century BC.

clue.text: Possible clue for S …

parts.note: in Morse code the letter S is three dots, so three dots in a row could clue S

explanation.surface: A crossword setter muses on how to clue the letter S.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing three dots are the point: printed dots like these are named by the answer, and dot dot dot spells S in Morse.
explanation.definitionFit: The three-dot punctuation mark has this name, and it matches the Morse signal for S.

clue.text: Assist old boy with coat heading to West Country

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means running right to left, so the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to assist is to aid
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh

explanation.surface: Helping a former pupil with a coat as he heads to the West Country of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Country' looks like the region of south-west England, but the phrase splits: 'heading to West' reverses AIDOBMAC, and 'Country' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a nation in south-east Asia.

clue.text: Damn your bra! All clothing comes off in this sort of relationship

indicators.note: each word loses its outer letters, its clothing, leaving only the inner ones

explanation.surface: A passionate lover curses a bra while the clothes come off.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a love affair, often a secret one.

clue.text: Silly dunderhead's rewritten lines

indicators.note: rewritten means the letters are put down again in a new order

parts.note: the head of dunder is its first letter, D

explanation.surface: A foolish blockhead has had his verses rewritten.
explanation.definitionFit: Idylls are short pastoral poems, so they are lines of verse, as in Tennyson's Idylls of the King.

clue.text: In enemy retreat with rifle shot cover here

indicators.note: the rearranged rifle covers, or goes around, the other pieces
shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters of rifle are jumbled
retreat means going backwards, so the word for enemy is reversed

parts.note: a foe is an enemy

explanation.surface: Under enemy fire, a soldier in retreat with a rifle seeks cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover' looks like part of the definition, but being in the line of fire means having none: it is the container signal, and 'here' alone defines, pointing to the spot the surface describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Here, where the shots are aimed, is the path a bullet takes, the place of greatest danger.

clue.text: Nest — having more than one would be rash

definitions.text: Nest — having more than one would be rash

parts.words: Nest — having more than one would be rash
parts.note: a bees' nest is the singular, and the plural is the name of an itchy skin rash, urticaria

explanation.surface: It would be reckless to own more than one nest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rash' reads as reckless but means a skin eruption: the plural of the answer is the common name for urticaria.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony of bees lives in this structure, their nest.

clue.text: Within a second, nosebag is empty

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its inside, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Within a second the horse's nosebag has been emptied.
explanation.definitionFit: Both prepositions mean in the midst of or inside a group.

clue.text: Whatever's like seeing a show on Broadway?

definitions.text: Whatever's like seeing a show on Broadway?

parts.words: Whatever's like seeing a show on Broadway?
parts.note: seeing a Broadway show is a typical New York activity, ..., and the whole word means whatever

explanation.surface: Someone asks what a Broadway show-going experience is like.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as A NY THING: NY is New York, home of Broadway.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatever and this word both mean any item at all, without restriction.

clue.text: Golf course reported wild animal

indicators.note: reported means spoken aloud, so the word for a golf course is taken by its sound

parts.note: links is a seaside golf course

explanation.surface: A wild cat was spotted on the golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A lynx is a wild cat with tufted ears, found in northern forests.

clue.text: Killer on the loose? Admit that's not so far-fetched

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the rearranged letters take in the abbreviation
on the loose means running free, so the letters of killer are scattered

parts.note: i.e., from Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A killer is at large; admit that it is plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: More likely is the comparative of probable, so less far-fetched.

clue.text: Perhaps heady years to begin with?

definitions.text: Perhaps heady years to begin with?

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of heady could be arranged some other way
to begin with means the first letter of the word years

explanation.surface: Wondering whether one's prime was a time of exciting years.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a golden period might be one's heady years.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's prime or peak period of success, often heady years indeed.

clue.text: Rejection of 7 down an abomination

indicators.note: an abomination is a monstrous thing, so the letters are made monstrous by rearrangement

parts.note: the answer to 7 down, a shop selling cooked meats

explanation.surface: Someone rejects a delicatessen as an abomination.
explanation.definitionFit: Denial is a refusal of a request, so a rejection.

clue.text: No granny may be free to kiss Nick or Tom's heads

indicators.note: may be signals that free can become another arrangement of its letters
heads means the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: No grandmother may be free to kiss Nick or Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'granny' is not a grandmother but a granny knot, the clumsy version of the answer, which is why the definition works.
explanation.definitionFit: A granny knot is a badly tied square knot; the correctly tied version is distinct from it, so not a granny.

clue.text: Part of me quit yearning for union

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone gives up longing for a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'for union' as the definition; 'for' only links the wordplay to it, so the definition is 'union'. Equity is the British actors' trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is the trade union representing British actors and performers.

clue.text: Coerce into serving the city

definitions.meaning: to force someone into service, originally as a sailor
the Chinese port, the country's largest city

explanation.surface: Press-ganging people into work for the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning to kidnap into a ship's crew, and the great Chinese city.

clue.text: The American leader is drunk and can't stand

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The US president is drunk and unable to stand up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can't stand' reads as too drunk to stay upright, but it means to loathe.
explanation.definitionFit: If you cannot stand something, you detest it.

clue.text: Near-perfect concept

indicators.note: near means almost, so the word for perfect falls one letter short

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: An almost flawless notion.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought or notion, which is a concept.

clue.text: Increase the minimum of unleaded petrol left in fuel tank

indicators.note: the least you can take of each word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The price of the little unleaded fuel left in the tank goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: An uplift is a rise, as in an uplift in sales.

clue.text: Participating in the regatta in Menton is a feat

indicators.note: participating in says the answer takes part in the words, lying within them

explanation.surface: Taking part in the boat race at Menton is an achievement.
explanation.walkthrough: Menton is a resort on the French Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: An attainment is an achievement, something accomplished, which is a feat.

clue.text: Port Suez returns endless money

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the letters are read in reverse
endless means each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An Egyptian port's revenues come back without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' leaves OR and UE; 'returns' reverses ORUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The euro is the currency used across much of the European Union.
